This game is amazing, and I haven't even gotten to the main storyline yet. There's this sort of adreneline rush while you're trying to hack your way in to someone's server and you only have a limited amount of time. Eventually I found myself rushing even when there wasn't a passive trace against me.
The beginning is rather intense, the tutorial really only gives you the bare bones and I am extremely glad I have a linux background because I went through the entire tutorial not reading it xD (although I found myself wishing I could grep, vim and when I upload I almost typed the entire scp command (scp :/home/[file]) .)

I found myself lost once... trying to remember whe- oh, it was when I had to reply to an email. Yeah, that wasn't explained very well at the beginning, but basically, you do what the email asks and you reply a blank email. The blank reply threw me off and I found myself trying to access things that had firewalls when I obviously had no capability of doing so [spoiler](you totally can actually, with analyze which is a command given all the way in the beginning (> man 2))[/spoiler]

The GUI is very helpful for those that aren't used to typing. I noticed that the tab complete didn't seem to work until I hit the tutorial for it, so for those that love pressing tab (like I do) and it doesn't work, don't panic, it comes later.

This game made me realize how vindictive I am; there is this one moment where you get hacked into and the GUI interface gets deleted. After I got back I immediately looked up the IP in my logs, went through the proxy server and then went to another server and deleted everything I could find on both server and proxy >_> probably didn't do anything but I got my GUI file back haha

*tl;dr?
Hacknet requires thinking and a lot of muscle memory which you'll get if you resort to typing out the commands (also pressing up like any linux terminal is a great shortcut) and there's a lot of side things you can do that really help pad the game. 
I love going through servers and reading the random forum/irc logs because they're all pretty funny. They aren't neccessarily relevant to the server you're on but it's an interesting little tidbit to read nonetheless. 
The music is also nice and subtle with a good beat that has it's highs and lows (I believe the music ingame is in the trailer).

There's a bit of a steep learning curve for people that have never programmed in their life but once you're past that it's a fun and exciting game.

Overall, it's a repetitive, but very visually and aurally satisfying, clicker/visual novel game. The best features are meant for multiplayer. You're warned to wipe logs early in the game, but logs are useless since there isnt anyone to read them (I stopped clearing them about halfway). Many of the features (like "forkbomb" and the trap functionality of the shells) are completely useless without multiplayer. There are no enemy hackers (save one, who is a major story character and only attempts to hack you once). The world is not alive. It is essentially a visual novel treasure hunt, where you go from one node to the next, doing the same things over and over with the incentive to just finish the game. The story and storytelling arent even good enough to justify it being this way. Maybe when it has multiplayer, itll be worth playing. Overall, the feeling of urgency isn't there like it would be if you were playing a game like slavehack.

When it gets multiplayer, if the multiplayer works correctly, it could well be one of the funnest and most exciting hacking games ever. Until then, unless you think the idea of writing commands instead of doing the same exact thing with a mouse is a good experience, I would probably just get uplink.

Also, if you're reading this review devs, Duckman should be expanded on. He's easily the best character in the game. Thanks Duckfam, you unsung hero.

I would try to put some kind of serious review here but there isn't a whole lot that can be said
that the steam page doesn't already say. It's a primarily keyboard controlled hacking simulator, in the same vein as Uplink. You're contacted by an unknown-to-you hacker named Bit, and set out on a journey through cyberspace with the HackNetOS, an operating system designed for many dubious reasons, eventually taking contract hacking jobs to earn a reputation among a few hacker groups.

The only downsides is that it's quite short. About 4-5 hours for my very first playthrough. The second problem is it just kind of ends. [spoiler] You and one of Bit's former friends V take down a server controlled by the people who were responsable for HackNet, followed by a final message or two from Bit, then the credits roll. The end.[/spoiler] 

That being said, it's simple concept managed to pull me into the story unfolding as you hack and crack your way through cyber security systems, trying to find out what Bit was up to and why he contacted you.

openCDTray actually opens CD tray.

And after completing the game I literally want to delete my operating system.

That's a signal of this game being super successful.
